title: Rewind from any input position
statement: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with states in $S$. Suppose there are states $r,s \in S$ and an optional destination state $d \in \mathrm{Option}(S)$ such that, for every input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols, state $r$ prescribes a left input-head move with successor state $s$, while state $s$ prescribes a left move with successor $s$ when an input symbol is scanned and a right move with successor $d$ when a blank is scanned; these actions write nothing on the work tapes, move no work-tape heads, and emit no output. From every configuration $c$ on input $x$ whose state is $r$, there exists $t \in \mathbb{N}$ such that after $t$ steps the configuration has state $d$ and input-head position $1$, with every other component equal to that of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A machine over the Boolean alphabet with states in $S$
For every input and work symbols, the transition from $r$ is the leftward control action to $s$
For every input and work symbols, the transition from $s$ is leftward to $s$ on a symbol and rightward to $d$ on a blank
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet on input
$x$, with a start state $r$, a scanning state $s$, and an optional dispatch
state $d$, such that regardless of the symbols read: from $r$ the machine
always moves the input head left and enters $s$; from $s$ it moves left and
stays in $s$ when an input symbol is scanned, and moves right and passes to
$d$ when a blank is scanned; and none of these transitions touches a work
tape or the output.  Then from any configuration $c$ in state $r$ there
exists a number of steps $t$ such that after $t$ steps the configuration
agrees with $c$ in every component except that its state is $d$ and its input
head is at position $1$.  This holds even when $x$ is empty or the input head
of $c$ starts at a boundary blank.
